answer: Add up the replication bill before the yield. Minting one identity costs a clean key, its own egress, and an answer written from scratch, a small sonnet of reasoning no sibling can reuse. Credit then arrives as a slow stream across eighty epochs, so a farm fronts the work long before the nectar lands. A rotating auditor pool reads each claim, and a lazy forge fails there rather than at payout. Copying a thousand agents costs a thousand original texts and a thousand waits.
